findings.claim: Rule A as literally written is sufficient for forgetting with its reported bound
findings.defect: A port in F may be selected as a next-frontier argument. Removing its sole current constraint existentially eliminates a retained output or a variable used below.
findings.witness: S(p0,p1,p2): NAE(p0,p1,p2), NAE(p0,p2,v), SELF(p1,u,v), with fresh own u,v
findings.required_fix: Exclude every selected-call argument from every peeling candidate, including ports in F; preserve original top identities in F updates.

findings.claim: Rule N follows from complement closure alone
findings.defect: Empty relations are complement-closed and rectangular. Every repeated cycle-word product must be nonempty.
findings.required_fix: State the alive/unfolding witness or explicit nonempty repeated-word hypothesis and the rectangular-product closure argument.

findings.claim: A frontier partition captures paths that climb back into the processed prefix
findings.reason: The partition records all prefix connectivity between frontier variables. Joining it with current components and restricting to the next frontier is exact when peeling is valid.

findings.claim: The generic S start repairs a main-conditioned certificate
findings.reason: The generic product theorem requires arbitrary S boundary variables, whereas a main-specific prefix can already disconnect them from main.

findings.claim: The bond-growth reading holds for targets that are copies of S
findings.defect: The earlier referee additionally requires ancestry after main consisting of S calls. Delayed S copies are not covered merely because their type is S.
findings.required_fix: State the full ancestry restriction and wrapper shift; distinguish relational H2 from the gap theorem.

findings.claim: Only direct or forced identity can sustain non-forgetting
findings.defect: N and A do not prove the forced-tie characterization, which the same note lists as future work.
findings.required_fix: Label the identity-only explanation as a working hypothesis.

counterexample.relation_boundary_convention: Selected continuation removed; no bottom support constraint imposed
counterexample.relation_formula: NAE(a,b,c) and d=b and NAE(a,c,f), for top(a,b,c), bottom(d,e,f)
counterexample.uniform_argument: Only 101 can continue from the odd row and only 010 from the even row because a constant intermediate triple violates the next block's first NAE. Complementary top rows remain disjoint for every power, so every power is nonrectangular.

validation.method: Fresh direct enumeration of all 8 top and 8 bottom triples, followed by set-based relational composition; independent symbolic argument for all powers
validation.scientific_independence: V2 same-task independent rederivation; no external replication
validation.initial_scratch_boundary_error_corrected: An initial calculation imposed bottom support and gave singleton rows. Final report uses the removed-continuation relation with 20 pairs and two-element rows.

strongest_surviving_result: Valid existential peeling plus boundary separation implies rectangularity; frontier partitions track all prefix connectivity; nonempty identity-cycle products obstruct forgetting.
next_discriminator: Verify both output-argument exclusion and original-top identity protection in the repaired transition, then require rejection of this counterexample.
